subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
options: Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the physical characteristics
They mean exactly the same thing
Genotype is the physical appearance; phenotype is the alleles
questions.explain: Genotype is the combination of alleles, while phenotype is the observable characteristic produced.

questions.q: Two heterozygous parents (Bb × Bb) are crossed. What is the expected ratio of dominant to recessive phenotypes in the offspring?
questions.explain: A Bb × Bb cross gives a 3:1 ratio of dominant to recessive phenotypes (BB, Bb, Bb, bb).

questions.q: Which structure carries the genetic information and is made of DNA?
questions.explain: Chromosomes are made of long DNA molecules that carry many genes coding for proteins.

questions.q: Different versions of the same gene are called:
questions.explain: Alleles are different forms of a gene, for example for eye colour.

questions.q: DNA is described as a polymer with what overall shape?
questions.explain: DNA is a double helix, two strands twisted together, made of repeating nucleotide units (a polymer).

questions.q: An organism with two identical alleles for a characteristic is described as:
questions.explain: Homozygous means having two identical alleles (e.g. BB or bb) for a gene.

questions.q: Gametes (sex cells) such as sperm and egg are described as haploid because they contain:
options: Half the normal number of chromosomes (23 in humans)
Twice the normal number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid, carrying a single set of chromosomes (23 in humans) so the full number is restored at fertilisation.

questions.q: Sickle cell disease is an inherited disorder caused by a recessive allele. A person who is a carrier:
options: Has one allele for it but does not show the disease, and can pass it on
Has the disease but cannot pass it on
Always shows symptoms of the disease
questions.explain: A carrier is heterozygous: they carry one recessive allele without showing the disorder but can pass it to offspring.

questions.q: A gene is best defined as:
options: A short section of DNA that codes for a protein
questions.explain: A gene is a small section of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a particular protein/characteristic.

questions.q: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. Two carrier parents (Ff × Ff) are crossed. What is the chance of a child having the disorder?
questions.explain: Two carriers (Ff × Ff) have a 1 in 4 chance of producing an affected ff child.

questions.q: When a haploid sperm fertilises a haploid egg, the resulting zygote is:
options: Diploid, with the full set of chromosomes restored
questions.explain: Fertilisation of two haploid gametes restores the diploid number, giving the zygote a full set of chromosomes.

questions.q: Meiosis produces:
questions.explain: Meiosis produces four non-identical haploid gametes, each with half the normal number of chromosomes.

questions.q: What is the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of that organism
questions.explain: The genome is the entire genetic material (all the DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are found in a normal human body cell?
questions.explain: Human body cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes (46 in total), one of each pair from each parent.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of variation caused mostly by the environment?
questions.explain: A scar is an environmental (acquired) variation, not caused by genes.

questions.q: Polydactyly (extra fingers/toes) is caused by a dominant allele. This means it:
options: Only appears when both alleles are present
Can be inherited from just one affected parent
questions.explain: As polydactyly is dominant, only one copy of the allele is needed, so one affected parent can pass it on.

questions.q: A recessive allele is only expressed in the phenotype when:
options: It is paired with a dominant allele
questions.explain: A recessive allele is only shown when both alleles are recessive, as a dominant allele would mask it.

questions.q: What determines whether a human baby is biologically male or female?
options: Whether the egg carries an X or Y chromosome
Whether the sperm carries an X or Y chromosome
questions.explain: Eggs always carry X; the sperm carries either X (giving XX, female) or Y (giving XY, male), so the sperm determines sex.

questions.q: A heterozygous brown-eyed parent (Bb) and a blue-eyed parent (bb) have children, where brown (B) is dominant. What ratio of brown to blue eyes is expected?
questions.explain: A Bb x bb cross gives Bb and bb offspring in equal numbers, a 1:1 ratio of brown to blue eyes.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a typical human male?
questions.explain: Human males have XY sex chromosomes, while females have XX.

questions.q: Which of these shows genetic variation rather than environmental variation?
options: A person being tanned after sunbathing
A plant grown in shade being taller and thinner
A footballer's strong leg muscles from training
questions.explain: Blood group is determined entirely by genes (genetic variation); the others are influenced by the environment.

questions.q: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
options: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and makes varied gametes; mitosis makes identical diploid cells
Mitosis makes gametes; meiosis makes body cells
questions.explain: Meiosis halves chromosome number to form varied gametes, whereas mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.
